description: Minimal Pony trait/interface model: two root traits, a trait that itself conforms, and conforming actor/class/primitive/struct/generic-class declarations across three files. Exercises type and member extraction, type->member CONTAINS, and — the reason the fixture exists (#6370) — the `is` conformance clause, including the other things Pony spells `is` which must NOT produce an edge.

expected_entities.name: Named
expected_entities.note: trait, declares no clause — the root everything else conforms to.

expected_entities.name: Loud
expected_entities.note: trait that ITSELF conforms — a trait is both a conformance target and a conforming type.

expected_entities.name: Box
expected_entities.note: `class Box[A: Any val] is Sized` — the generic parameter list the anchor must cross.

expected_entities.name: Plain
expected_entities.note: NO `is` clause — the negative control. Its body contains the identity operator `this is other`.

expected_entities.name: Checker
expected_entities.note: No clause; its body holds `a is b` and a STRING containing a whole fake declaration.

expected_relationships.note: #6370: `class Circle is Named`, the plain single-trait form on a class.

#6370: FIRST member of `is (Named & Sized)`. A producer that takes only the first name of an intersection list — which is exactly what the graphql YAML pack did for `A & B` — passes this row and fails the next.
#6370: SECOND member of the same list. This is the only row in the fixture that grades the multi-type split.
#6370: `class Box[A: Any val] is Sized`. The only row that fails when the anchor does not cross a generic parameter list — every other conforming type here is non-generic.
#6370: owner keyword `actor`. Rows here vary the DECLARATION KEYWORD and hold the clause shape constant, so a producer hard-coded to `class` fails this, Zero and Point but keeps Circle.
#6370: owner keyword `struct`, and the only actors.pony row whose target is Sized rather than Named.

#6370: owner keyword `trait`, and the only row where owner and target are declared in the SAME file — so it also grades that the edge is anchored on the TYPE rather than on the file, which from_file narrowing could not otherwise distinguish.

Pre-existing pony behaviour, held so the fixture measures more than the one edge kind #6370 adds — and so a regression that dropped ALL embedded relationships is distinguishable from one that dropped only IMPLEMENTS.
Pre-existing pony behaviour on the type that has NO conformance clause: Plain must keep its member edges while acquiring no IMPLEMENTS.
Pre-existing pony behaviour: a behaviour (`be`) member, on the type that also carries an IMPLEMENTS.

forbidden_relationships.note: #6370 OVER-FIRING, identity operator: `this is other` in Plain.same() is Pony's reference-equality test, not a declaration. Plain has NO clause of its own, so a producer that searches FORWARD from the declaration for `is` instead of anchoring at the name lands on exactly this. FIRES, verified: deleting the `^` from ponyIsAnchorRE and searching produces Plain -> other.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, identity operator in a SECOND file: `a is b` in Checker.check(). FIRES, verified: the same searching mutant produces both this and Plain -> other, in different files, and the gate reports exactly those two forbidden hits. Two rows rather than one because they fail together only if the defect is general; a producer special-cased to shapes.pony would keep this one.

#6370 OVER-FIRING: Plain declares no conformance at all. Pony gives every type an implicit `Any` supertype, but nothing in the SOURCE says Named, and this extractor must report what is written. NOT FIRED by any mutant tried, stated plainly rather than implied: the searching mutant binds Plain to `other`, the identifier its body actually contains, not to a trait. This is an absence fence for a producer that DEFAULTS a clause-less type to a root, which is a shape no single edit of this extractor produces.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, string literal: Checker.doc() returns the STRING "class Spectre is Phantom". NOT FIRED by the searching mutant, and the reason is worth knowing before copying this fixture: that mutant takes the FIRST `is` after the declaration, and Checker's first is `a is b` one method earlier — the row above is what it trips. This row fences a producer that emits EVERY `is` in a declaration, or one with no anchor at all. This extractor has no string awareness; the anchor is the whole guard, stated plainly rather than implied. A YAML rule-pack producer WOULD fire here, which is what internal/engine/rules/graphql/frameworks/graphql_schema.yaml does for a commented-out SDL type.

#6370 OVER-FIRING, direction: Loud conforms to Named, not the reverse. NOT FIRED by any mutant of this extractor, and it cannot be — the edge is EMBEDDED on the owning record, so its source is the record it sits on and no single edit can transpose it. It is an absence fence for a producer that names source and target by capture group, which is a rule-pack shape rather than an extractor one; that exact defect is live today in internal/engine/rules/kotlin/frameworks/kmp.yaml (#6805). It is the only fixture row that would survive a whole-file edge count, which is why it is here despite being unfireable from this side.

forbidden_entities.name: Ghost
forbidden_entities.note: #6370: `// class Ghost is Phantom` is COMMENTED OUT in actors.pony. NOT REACHABLE by any mutant of this extractor, stated plainly rather than implied: typeDeclarationRE is `(?m)^(actor|class|…)` with no leading-whitespace allowance, so a `//` before the keyword makes the line structurally unmatchable and no loosening of the `is` clause can reach it. Kept as an absence fence for a rule-pack producer. The REACHABLE versions of this hazard are real defects and are pinned instead as TestPonyHierarchy_DeclarationInsideCommentOrDocstringOverFires_KnownDivergence: the same declaration at column 0 inside a /* */ block comment, inside a type's own """ docstring, or inside a """ docstring in a method body IS extracted in all three cases, entity and edge alike. It is deliberately not in this fixture, because a golden fixture must stay green.

forbidden_entities.name: Phantom
forbidden_entities.note: #6370: the trait named in that same commented-out line. Same grading status as the row above — an unreachable fence, not a mutant-killed row.

forbidden_entities.name: Spectre
forbidden_entities.note: #6370: the type named inside Checker.doc()'s string literal. Unreachable for the same structural reason — the string sits on an INDENTED line, and typeDeclarationRE requires column 0.
